basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'Vers. 21. Deprecatus est pro sua uxore. Dominus promiserat Abrahae quod multiplicaret'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 21. Deprecatus est pro sua uxore. Dominus promiserat Abrahae quod multiplicaret semen ejus sicut stellas coeli et sicut arenam maris. Quae multiplicatio per Isaac futura erat, juxta quod Abrahae | dictum est: In Isaac vocabitur tibi semen. Quid ergo est quod Isaac sterilem uxorem sortitus est, si per eum semen Abrahae multiplicandum erat? Sed sciendum quia sancti ea quae orando obtinent sic praedestinata sunt ut precibus impetrent. Hinc est quod per Isaac multiplicandum erat semen Abrahae: sed hoc ipsum orando obtinuit. Nam et omnibus justis praeparatum est ante saecula regnum Dei, sed ita ut orando et laborando ad illud suo tempore perveniant.
